# caliper-docgen-semantic

## 0.4.0

- With the experimental TypeScript checker on, a function prop keeps the optional and rest markers its parameters are written with. antd's `Progress.format` reads `(percent?: number, successPercent?: number) => ReactNode` and `ActionButton.close` reads `(...args: any[]) => void`; the checker's answer used to lose the markers, giving `(percent: undefined | number, …)` and `(args: any[]) => void`, which changes how a call site reads.
- With the experimental TypeScript checker on, a prop whose type is a name that does not resolve (an import that cannot be found, a name declared nowhere) is no longer reported as `any`. It is `opaque` and carries `degradedBy: ["unresolvableImport"]`, so a reader can tell it from a prop written as `any`.
- With the experimental TypeScript checker on, a prop whose name starts with two underscores keeps the name the source writes. Mantine's `__size`, `__vars` and `__clearable` used to come back as `___size`, `___vars` and `___clearable` (the checker keeps such names with a third underscore), so those props appeared under a name nobody wrote.
- The experimental TypeScript checker can now run on `tsrs` (`npm i tsrs`) as well as on `typescript@beta`. Caliper finds `node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs` when no `typescript` 7.1 is installed, and `--tsc-path` (or `tscPath`) also takes the `@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs` binary, which used to fail with "could not determine tsc's version". Only the `tsrs` build that was checked against Caliper is accepted (`0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`); any other `tsrs` release is refused with the usual warning until it has been checked. On Chakra, Caliper's output was identical to the one from `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. The checker is still off by default.
- The minimum supported Rust version is now 1.99, and the crates use edition 2024. Building from source needs Rust 1.99 or newer; prebuilt binaries and npm packages are unaffected, and the output is unchanged.
- Agents reading TOON output no longer lose what they need to write a valid call. A literal union such as shadcn's `size` or `variant` now lists every value instead of ending in `...(+2)`, function props keep their parameter names (`(value: string, index?: number) => void`), a prop's `@deprecated`, `@see` and `@since` notes appear in a `tags` column, and a discriminated union names its discriminant in a `discriminant:` line. TOON is about 12% longer on antd and shadcn; unions of types past 8 members and intersections past 4 are still cut, with the count.
- Prop types now keep more of what TypeScript says about them. Tuples keep their optional and rest elements and their labels: `[string, ...number[]]` used to print as `[string, number[][]]`, and `[head: string, ...tail: number[]]` used to come out partly unreadable. A spread of a known tuple, `[string, ...Tail]`, is flattened as TypeScript does. Bigint literals (`10n`), negative number literals (`-1`), `unique symbol`, enum members (`Size.Small`, offered to Storybook as its value `"small"`) and template literal patterns (`` `${number}px` ``) are represented instead of being marked opaque. An object type with several call signatures, a `new` signature, or a call signature beside properties keeps them all, and a recursive alias such as `type Json = string | Json[]` refers back to itself by name instead of being cut off. A getter is read as a property (`get size(): number` is `readonly size: number`), not as a method.

  The JSON output moves to schema version 5. A tuple's elements are now `{ "type", "label"?, "modifier"? }` objects, the type kinds `bigintLiteral`, `uniqueSymbol`, `enumMember`, `templateLiteral`, `callable`, `recursive` and `truncated` are new, and the `templateLiteral` reason of an `opaque` type is gone. Update `caliper-docgen`, the Vite plugin and the Storybook addon together; a mismatched install stops with a message naming both versions.

## 0.3.0

- The experimental on-demand TypeScript 7.1 checker now works with any 7.1 release (beta, rc or stable) instead of only `7.1.0-beta`, replaces its `tsc` process when it grows past 768 MiB between requests, and no longer makes closing a session wait for a request in progress. For library users: `PINNED_VERSIONS` is now `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`, and `expected_versions` entries may be a `major.minor` series such as `"7.1"`.

A type that recurses (including an alias of an array or tuple of itself) is marked as a reference back to itself, while `Box<Box<string>>` stays two nested objects; a callback keeps its optional parameters even when it is written through an alias, and a callback whose parameters cannot be read is marked as degraded instead of being given required ones. A type cut at a depth or size limit is marked `truncated` instead of standing in as the checker's text. A type from a dependency (an interface, or an object alias) stays a name; the TypeScript lib's utilities such as `Partial` and `Record` are expanded. # 0026. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax

**Status:** Accepted (2026-11-08) **Date:** 2026-11-07

## Context

ADR 0006 and 0007 made the TypeScript checker an opt-in second resolver, because a whole-project `tsc` run cost up to 9.3 s and 975 MiB (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`); ADR 0022 bounded it to a warm per-component request. The structural default still answers wrong without a marker: a type that is only a call signature becomes `{}`, `Omit`, `Pick` and `Partial` reached through an alias lose their effect, and a factory's props are taken from a name-matched interface (`docs/rdt-differences.md`, classes 4 to 6). A prototype found more: `[string, ...number[]]` prints as `[string, number[][]]` and a getter reads as a method. Each fix is another rule in a resolver that re-implements the type system.

tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. A throwaway prototype through the Node client (not in the repository; these numbers are the record) measured on Chakra `ButtonProps` (1,138 props) a 43-47 ms snapshot and the first converted prop at 62-67 ms, where ADR 0022 measured 703 ms with `tsc` on a different program root (indicative, not an A/B), with tsrs peaking at 126-130 MiB. On 16 hand-written components the checker was equal or better on 14, worse on union member order and an unresolvable import. A polymorphic component instantiated through a virtual file gave 267 props for `'div'` where both engines give 2 today. tsrs's own benchmark (`bench/RESULTS.md`) reports 1.8 to 4.2 times TypeScript 7.1 beta's speed and 2.1 to 2.6 times less memory.

## Decision

The checker decides types and oxc decides syntax.

- **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.
- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` or a config option turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` give way to it.
- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint is re-measured with tsrs in S4. The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).
- **Pin.** We pin an exact tsrs build (`0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta` today) and bump it on purpose. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.

# Gate measurements

**Last measured:** 2026-11-09 on `feat/gate-harness` at `f3784be5`, tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta` (the pin), macOS 27.3 on an Apple M5 Max (18 cores, 64 GiB). Two of the gates in [ADR 0026](adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md#gates-before-the-default-flips) need a measurement rather than a test: determinism on a large program and memory past 600 edits. This records how each was made measurable and what it read.

Rerun both with `just gate-measure` (about 17 minutes). It builds the large project outside the repository (`GATE_FIXTURES`, default `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large`, by `scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs`), builds `crates/semantic/examples/gate_harness.rs`, and prints one JSON line per gate. A run that fails its own check exits 1.

## The program

- `scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs` installs `@chakra-ui/react` 3.37.0 and `@mui/material` 9.5.0 (the root `package.json`'s pins) with `pnpm`, and writes one wrapper per exported component, `export function ChakraButton(props: ComponentProps<typeof Button>)`: 1,616 components (1,466 Chakra, 150 MUI). The Chakra and MUI sources themselves were not fetched, so this is not the Chakra corpus of `docs/measurement.md`: it is what an app that wraps both libraries asks the checker.
- Each request to the checker builds a program that loads one library's declarations whole, which is what makes it a large program.
- The harness uses the session a Storybook addon runs: a lazy `WatchSession` with `load_dependencies` on, nothing collapsed, and a warm `OnDemand` that waits up to 120 s, over the pinned tsrs binary the oracle's `tsrs-bin.ts` resolves.

## Memory past 600 edits

- **How.** `OnDemand` now counts its planned process replacements by cause (`recycles()`: `worn` after 64 programs, `bloated` after `max_rss_mib`) and reports the process that answered last (`process_id()`); each replacement is logged at debug level. The harness rewrites one component's file (`ButtonProps & { edit{n}: string }`, which makes the checker load Chakra), calls `update_file`, asks for the component, and reads the process's PID and resident memory from `ps` after every answer, 650 times. It then asks a fresh session over the final files and compares the two answers whole.
- **Result at the shipped bound (768 MiB):** 650 of 650 answers came from the checker and carried that edit's prop (0 stale). The checker ran as 11 processes, 10 replacements, all `worn` and none `bloated`. Peak resident memory was 446 MiB (452 MiB in an earlier run of the same command). The last answer equals the fresh session's.
- **What that shows, and what it does not.** The 64-program limit does the work on this program: a process reached 446 MiB at most, so the 768 MiB bound never fired. The gate asks for the bound to be exercised, so the harness takes `--max-rss-mib`. With 300: 49 `bloated` replacements, 50 processes, no `worn`, peak 331 MiB (a request that grows past the bound finishes first, and the check runs on every fourth request), and the last answer equals the fresh session's again.
- **Verdict: PASS** for what was measured (no leak past 650 edits, replacements keep the answers right, the memory bound works when crossed). Not measured: a program whose single process passes 768 MiB on its own, or a real watch session with the Storybook addon and Node in the loop.

## Determinism across checker counts

- **Not applicable as worded.** tsrs has no checker-count option on the path caliper uses. `tsrs --api --help` lists `-async`, `-callbacks`, `-cwd`, `-pipe`, `-runExternalCode`, `-timing` and `-useCaseSensitiveFileNames`, and `--api --checkers 2` is refused with `flag provided but not defined: -checkers`. The compile mode (`tsrs --checkers 2 -p .`) takes the flag, as `typescript@7.1.0-beta`'s `tsc --help --all` documents, but caliper never runs it: `supervisor.rs` starts `--api --async --cwd` and the checker pool's size is the server's own. No `tsrs` string names a count either.
- **Nearest measurable form.** The output must not depend on how the checker's parallelism is set, on the order components are asked in, or on which process answers. The harness asks a fresh tsrs process for 150 components (every tenth of the 1,616, sorted by key) with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` set to 1, 2 and 4, three runs each, the middle run asking in reverse order, and byte-compares all nine outputs (each component's JSON entry and diagnostics, sorted by key). The variable changes the process: its thread count read 4, 5 and 7 at 1, 2 and 4. It does not change a checker count, which nothing here sets.
- **Result:** all nine outputs are identical, 341,396,960 bytes each. 148 of the 150 components were answered by the checker in every run; `MuiPopoverRoot` and `MuiSliderMark` kept their structural answer in every run (why the checker declined them was not investigated). So the checker's answers are identical across thread counts, runs, process restarts and query order.
- **Verdict: NOT MEASURABLE as worded; PASS in the nearest form.** The ADR's wording should read "output is deterministic across repeated runs, thread counts, restarts and query order on a large program" until tsrs exposes a count on `--api`. The compile-mode flag was not tried against a program, since its output is not what caliper reads.

## Not covered

- Other platforms: both measurements ran on macOS arm64. The Linux CI run is a separate gate.
- Wall time was not part of the question; a run takes about 0.5 s per edit here.
- The per-edit `ps` sampling reads the answering process after its reply, so a process that peaked inside a request and shrank before the sample is under-read.

input.message:
Both gates were measured with commands I ran. Gate B (memory) PASS. Gate A (determinism) is NOT MEASURABLE as worded and PASS in the nearest form.

- **Gate B, memory past 600 edits:** `just gate-measure` drove 650 rewrite-then-ask edits through a lazy `WatchSession` with a warm `OnDemand` over the pinned tsrs 0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta, on a 1,616-component Chakra+MUI wrapper project.
  - All 650 answers came from the checker and carried that edit's prop. The checker ran as 11 processes with 10 `worn` and 0 `bloated` recycles, peak RSS 446 MiB, and the final answer equals a fresh session's.
  - At the shipped 768 MiB bound, the 64-program limit does all the recycling and the RSS bound never fires. To exercise it I ran `--max-rss-mib 300`: 49 `bloated` recycles, 50 processes, no `worn`, peak 331 MiB, final answer equal to fresh.
- **Gate A, determinism across checker counts:** tsrs's `--api` has no checker-count flag. `--api --checkers 2` is refused with "flag provided but not defined"; only compile mode takes `--checkers`, and caliper never runs that.
  - The nearest form was `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` 1, 2 and 4, three fresh processes each, one run in reverse query order, on 150 components. All 9 outputs were byte-identical at 341,396,960 bytes. The tsrs process's thread count read 4, 5 and 7 across the settings, so the variable does change parallelism, but it is not a checker count.
  - 148 of 150 components were answered by the checker; `MuiPopoverRoot` and `MuiSliderMark` kept their structural answer in every run. I did not investigate why the checker declined them.
- **Deliverables:**
  - `OnDemand::recycles()` (worn and bloated counts), `OnDemand::process_id()` and a debug log line on each replacement, with unit tests against the fake tsc. I added a minor changeset for `caliper-docgen-semantic` because these are new public API; they are invisible to the CLI and the addon.
  - `crates/semantic/examples/gate_harness.rs` (about 170 lines, over your 60 to 100, because it holds both gates) and `scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs`. The fixtures script recreates the large project under `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large` from the pinned Chakra and MUI packages, offline-preferred.
  - A `just gate-measure` recipe, about 17 minutes.
  - `docs/gate-measurements.md`, linked from ADR 0026's gates section. I did not reword the ADR's determinism bullet. I suggest it read "deterministic across repeated runs, thread counts, restarts and query order".
- **Checks, all exit 0:** `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-semantic --locked`.
  - The new tests failed to compile with the `src` files reverted, then passed once restored.
  - A clean-room worktree under `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/clean-gate-harness` (pnpm frozen install, semantic nextest, release build and a 70-edit harness run) was fine; I removed it afterwards.
- **Not verified:** a single process passing 768 MiB on its own, a real Storybook plus Node session, Linux or Windows, the compile-mode `--checkers` flag against a program, and the full `just test` suite. This is not the Chakra corpus of `docs/measurement.md` (large corpora were not fetched).
- **Branch `feat/gate-harness`**, pushed, linked to trail #259, three signed commits: `b84e7df1` (feat counter), `f3784be5` (harness), `41b279bd` (docs).
